name: Hermes Agent

surfaces.label: Hermes Desktop (Electron). Turns do NOT run in this process: they run in a `hermes serve` Python backend the app spawns or attaches to. Bundle name is inconsistent in the vendor tree: Hermes.app (installer docs and update code) vs Hermes Agent.app (product-identity.cjs, bundled variant).

Messaging gateway (`hermes gateway run`). On macOS a launchd job, label ai.hermes.gateway or ai.hermes.gateway-<profile>, plist ~/Library/LaunchAgents/<label>.plist. Tree: osascript -> sh -> python wrapper (hermes_cli.stderr_timestamp) -> python gateway run.

Headless backend `hermes serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0 [--profile P]` that Hermes Desktop spawns (or attaches to; one per host). `hermes mcp serve` (a stdio MCP bridge that other agents such as Claude Code or Cursor spawn as a helper, not an agent turn runner) is excluded by the argv token `mcp`.
Legacy Desktop backend `python -m hermes_cli.main dashboard --no-open` (older runtimes fall back to it) and the user-run `hermes dashboard` web UI (chat is served over /api/pty).
ACP server for Zed, VS Code, JetBrains: `hermes-acp` launcher or `python -m acp_adapter`
ACP server started as the `hermes acp` subcommand

Hermes CLI and TUI (`hermes`, `hermes --tui`). ps shows the store Python interpreter running an inline `-I -c` (source install) or `-P -c` (bundled payload) bootstrap that imports hermes_cli.main, not a process called hermes. TUI tree: this python -> node --expose-gc .../dist/entry.js -> python -m tui_gateway.entry (the agent lives in the last one).
Fallback: a process titled `hermes`. Only when the optional setproctitle package is installed, which then also hides all argv from ps. Not shipped by default.

session_store.note: One SQLite database (WAL mode) per profile home, shared by CLI, TUI, Desktop, gateway, cron and ACP. Not one file per session, so there is no per_session path. HERMES_HOME moves it. Tables sessions and messages hold the private conversation: read only session_turn_leases, gateway_heartbeats and sessions metadata columns. JSONL appears only as an emergency spill at ~/.hermes/sessions/<id>.jsonl when state.db was replaced under a live process.

working_signals.name: state.db-wal mtime
working_signals.meaning: Weak and database-wide, not per session: any Hermes process writing any session moves the WAL mtime. Messages are flushed per tool round and at turn end, and last_activity_at heartbeats about every 60 s, so a long model stream shows no writes. The reference probe cannot evaluate this (no per_session path), so it is inert there.

Inferred and uncalibrated: no Hermes process was available to measure idle versus streaming. Sum over the whole tree, including the Node renderer and the tui_gateway child. Misses a turn that is only waiting on the network.

x_precise_working_signal.note: Not expressible in the schema's working_signals enum. Proposed new kind: sqlite_row. Read-only query against each state.db (default and every profiles/*/state.db).
x_precise_working_signal.query: SELECT holder, conversation_id, expires_at FROM session_turn_leases WHERE expires_at > strftime('%s','now')
x_precise_working_signal.meaning: A non-expired row means a turn is running right now. The row is taken when run_conversation starts and deleted when it ends, so it is per turn, not per open session. TTL 300 s, refreshed every 60 s, so a SIGKILLed holder leaves a row for up to 5 minutes: also require the holder pid to be alive.
x_precise_working_signal.pid_to_process: pid is the process running the agent: the hermes python for the classic CLI, the tui_gateway python (grandchild of the outer hermes) for the TUI, the hermes serve backend for Desktop and dashboard chat, the gateway process for messaging. Walk up to the matching surface. Turns in a compute-host child may name that child pid.
x_precise_working_signal.session_mapping: conversation_id is the compression-lineage root session id; the turn= part of holder is the live session id. Subagents take their own rows with platform=subagent.
x_precise_working_signal.gateway_shortcut:
~/.hermes/gateway_state.json (and profiles/

/gateway_state.json): active_agents > 0 with gateway_state running or degraded means the gateway is busy (foreground turns + cron jobs + API runs). Stale after 120 s without updated_at.

waiting_signals.meaning: A dangerous-command approval (once/session/always/deny) is about to be asked of the human. Observer hook, so a shell hook or plugin has to write the marker. Paired with post_approval_response, which carries the choice (deny, timeout, cancelled).

clarify, sudo and secret questions have no hook and no marker on disk. In TUI and Desktop they are server-to-client JSON-RPC requests (approval, clarify, sudo, secret) held open on the tui_gateway connection, invisible from outside. While blocked, the turn lease stays held and refreshed, so the lease query keeps saying working.

hooks.config:
Shell hooks: `hooks:` block in ~/.hermes/config.yaml (per profile: ~/.hermes/profiles/

/config.yaml), each entry {matcher, command, timeout, fail_closed}; first-use consent stored in ~/.hermes/shell-hooks-allowlist.json (bypass: --accept-hooks, HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS=1, hooks_auto_accept: true). Python plugin hooks: ~/.hermes/plugins// via ctx.register_hook, enabled in plugins.enabled. Gateway-only hooks: ~/.hermes/hooks//HOOK.yaml + handler.py (trusted by placement). Signed HTTP webhooks: `hooks.outbound:` list in ~/.hermes/config.yaml. Inspect with `hermes hooks list|test|revoke|doctor`.
hooks.note: Turn boundaries: pre_llm_call fires once per turn before the loop; on_session_end fires at each turn finalization (canonical payload has completed, failed, interrupted, turn_exit_reason), NOT only when the session closes; post_llm_call fires only for successful, non-interrupted turns. Shell hooks get JSON on stdin and follow the Claude Code wire shape (exit 2 or {decision:block} blocks pre_tool_call). Full list is VALID_HOOKS in hermes_cli/plugins.py; the gateway:* names apply only to messaging sessions.

telemetry.how: Opt-in, gateway and cron only. config.yaml monitoring.gateway_health_export.enabled and monitoring.export.otlp {enabled, endpoint, headers_env}, OTLP/HTTP, needs the `otlp` extra (opentelemetry-sdk 1.39.1). Exports gateway up/state/busy/active_agents/background_work gauges, gateway.lifecycle spans and content-free warning logs. Never prompts, messages or tool data. No OTEL_* environment variables are read, and CLI, TUI and Desktop turns are not exported. Rich per-turn traces are a separate path: the observer hooks (telemetry_schema_version hermes.observer.v1), a Langfuse plugin, and NeMo Relay. Check with `hermes monitoring status`.

sources.claim: Lease renewal is not evidence of progress, and a dead-pid holder is reclaimed only on proof the pid is gone. CORRECTED in verification: a stalled turn does not renew forever by default, because a liveness watchdog (agent.turn_liveness.timeout_s, default 600 s, 0 disables) aborts a turn with no activity and stops the refresher, so the row can still read as working for up to about 600 s of stall plus up to 300 s of TTL

notes: Every claim comes from the vendor's public source at commit 6ffe3b2 (2026-09-29) and its docs site; nothing was run because Hermes is not installed here, so confidence cannot exceed documented. Best turn signal is the session_turn_leases row (see x_precise_working_signal), which the schema cannot express yet; it is missing for agents with persistence disabled and can lag a wedged turn by up to about 15 minutes (600 s liveness watchdog plus 300 s TTL). Do not key on process name `hermes` or on caffeinate. The generic tui surface matches the python interpreter by argv, so it also catches one-shot `hermes chat -q` runs (cron, kanban workers) and any process whose argv mentions hermes_cli.main. Surface order matters for the reference probe (first match wins): gateway, serve, dashboard and acp surfaces come before the generic one, and the generic one excludes them by exact argv token. Misfiling is by SUBSTRING, not by whole word: args_contain is a substring test, so any argv token containing gateway, serve, dashboard or acp_adapter (a prompt saying 'server' or 'preserve', `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway.py`) is filed under that surface. `hermes mcp serve` is excluded on purpose because other agents spawn it as a helper. The GUI path match is /Hermes.app/Contents/MacOS/Hermes, which an unrelated Pandora client called Hermes would also satisfy: confirm com.nousresearch.* in Info.plist before trusting it. The fallback surface names=[hermes] is unreachable in a default install (setproctitle is not a dependency) and would also match any other executable called hermes; it is kept only for hand-configured installs. Canary and commit desktop builds are named 'Hermes Canary.app' / 'Hermes <sha7>.app' and are not covered by path_contains. The reference probe splits ps output on spaces, so 'Hermes Agent.app' paths cannot match there. Verified 2026-09-29 by an adversarial pass: see registry/evidence/hermes.md section Verification.
